cover_letter:
Dear Vinta team,

I am excited to apply for the Product Marketing Specialist position. Vinta's focus on helping US startups build modern, user-centered products, especially in healthcare, matches the way I work: understand the audience and the product deeply, turn that understanding into clear positioning, and connect marketing, sales, and delivery around measurable outcomes.

At Wipro's Meta project, I translated global product updates into value propositions, pitches, playbooks, and enablement programs for 150+ Meta Marketing Pros. I led adoption of native AI in CRM workflows, increasing daily usage by 150%, and designed a bootcamp that reduced time-to-productivity by 50% while achieving 90% CSAT. This experience taught me how to make complex technical capabilities useful and actionable for commercial teams.

I also bring hands-on demand generation experience. At Munzner, I built a 10-stage email nurture funnel that attracted 10,000+ visits and generated approximately R$50,000 in high-ticket revenue. An inbound content program produced 100 qualified leads from organic traffic. As co-founder of Meu Barzin, I defined an ICP and B2B value proposition, captured 505 qualified leads, conducted qualitative discovery, and used funnel data to identify a 43.9% first-message dropout.

I would bring Vinta a structured, curious, and highly collaborative approach to messaging, campaigns, research, and sales enablement. I would welcome the opportunity to discuss how my product, marketing, and technical-services background can support Vinta's growth in healthcare and other industries.

Best regards,
Kevin Augusto Vieira

form_answers.question: Why are you interested in Vinta and this Product Marketing role?
form_answers.answer: Vinta operates where product thinking, technical complexity, and customer outcomes meet. That is the environment in which I do my best work. My experience translating Meta product updates into sales messaging and enablement, combined with hands-on inbound and B2B product work, would let me help Vinta make its value clear to different industries and buyer personas. I am especially interested in healthcare because user-centered product communication must respect both usability and the complexity of the domain.

form_answers.question: Tell us about a go-to-market or demand-generation initiative you led.
form_answers.answer: At Munzner, I launched the company's first digital course as an entry product and built a 10-stage automated email nurture funnel in Bitrix24 and Sendpulse. The funnel attracted more than 10,000 visits and converted approximately 10 enrollments into around R$50,000 in high-ticket revenue. I also wrote roughly 10 technical blog articles that generated 1,000 organic visits and 100 qualified leads. I used the results to refine content themes, messaging, and the path from first touch to conversion.

form_answers.question: What is your experience with ABM and audience segmentation?
form_answers.answer: My documented experience is strongest in ICP definition, audience segmentation, B2B partner targeting, and account-specific outreach rather than owning a formal ABM program under that name. At Meu Barzin, I defined the target partner profile, mapped the value proposition for local businesses, prioritized high-potential accounts, and led direct outreach that secured pilot partnerships. I would apply the same discipline to ABM at Vinta: define account tiers, align messaging to buying committees, coordinate marketing and sales touchpoints, and measure engagement, pipeline coverage, conversion, and deal quality.

form_answers.question: How do you turn research and metrics into marketing decisions?
form_answers.answer: I combine qualitative and quantitative signals. At Meu Barzin, interviews and funnel mapping revealed partner-density and API-latency issues, including a 43.9% first-message dropout. That finding changed the product and messaging priorities. In the Meta project, I used Power BI, Excel, call listening, and root-cause analysis to identify knowledge and adoption gaps, then created enablement interventions. I use metrics to locate the problem and customer conversations to understand why it exists.
